solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Publisher's device: it shuts in hour after work

indicators.note: something that shuts in another thing encloses it, so the colon goes round the rest

parts.note: 'it' points back to the punctuation mark just printed in the clue, a colon

indicators.note: 'after' puts the hour behind the work in the order of letters

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A publisher's emblem described as a mechanism that locks in an hour once work is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The ':' in the clue is itself the colon that 'it' refers to; 'after' places H behind OP before the colon closes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's emblem or imprint printed on a book's title page or spine carries this name.

clue.text: Opportunity Dutch ancestors grabbed

indicators.note: the run of letters is grabbed, held inside the words Dutch ancestors

explanation.surface: A lucky break that some Dutch forebears seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed' signals that the answer sits inside 'Dutch ancestors', spanning the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunity is a chance, a favourable moment to do something.

clue.text: Brought up to be disagreeable person society shuns

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to repel is to be disagreeable or repugnant to someone

explanation.surface: Someone raised to be unpleasant ends up an outcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' looks like upbringing, but in a down entry it reverses REPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an outcast avoided by everyone is called this, after sufferers of the disease once shunned.

clue.text: Where sportswriters sit and sweat, getting cross with crowds all round

indicators.note: all round says the crowds word encircles the other pieces

parts.note: to crowd is to press, so crowds gives presses
BO, body odour, is what sweat produces
X is the cross-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Journalists in their seats perspire and grow annoyed with the surrounding crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweat' and 'cross' look like the journalists' discomfort, but both are wordplay: body odour and the cross-shaped letter, with 'all round' wrapping the crowds word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters at a stadium are seated in enclosed areas reserved for the media.

clue.text: Name O. Henry originally adopted for theatrical work

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: The writer O. Henry's name taken up for a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical Japanese drama, with masks, music and dance, is a form of theatre.

clue.text: American handbag contains what's acceptable to carry on

indicators.note: contains has the handbag word holding the other letter

parts.note: in American English a woman's handbag is a purse
U means upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: A US handbag holds whatever is permitted as cabin luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on' looks like hand baggage; it is the definition, meaning continue. U for 'acceptable' is the old upper-class label.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going with a course or activity is to follow it through, continue.

clue.text: Wellington got going as stud

indicators.note: going says the letters of got leave the boot word

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot, also called a gumboot

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington got moving like a stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the Duke; it is the boot. The letters G, O, T of 'got' go from it, scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: The central boss on a shield is a raised knob, a stud.

clue.text: Became dim and indignant

definitions.meaning: a window or glasses that cloud over with condensation become dim

explanation.definitionFit: Glass misted by vapour grows dim; a person boiling with anger is likewise described with this phrase.

clue.text: African with English typing a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An African writer typing a novel in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being typed; it is the anagram signal for E, TYPING and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the country of the Nile and the pyramids, in north-east Africa.

clue.text: According to a rule all people like this fruit

indicators.note: following a fixed rule: take the first letter and then every third one

explanation.surface: A claim that, by some law, everyone enjoys this fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to a rule' signals a regular pick: letters 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13 of 'all people like'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard fruit, round with crisp flesh, the one in the Eden story.

clue.text: Where berry bush can be cultivated

definitions.text: Where berry bush can be cultivated

indicators.note: cultivating works the ground over, so the letters of berry bush are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardening note on where a berry-bearing shrub might be grown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: 'can be cultivated' rearranges BERRY BUSH, and a bed of shrubs is exactly where one grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area of shrubs is the natural place for a fruiting bush to be grown.

clue.text: Petty officer everyone looked after

parts.note: SM is short for sergeant major
everyone means all
minded means looked after, as a babysitter minds children

explanation.surface: A petty officer whom the whole crew watched over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty officer' reads as a naval rank, but 'Petty' alone is the definition and 'officer' gives SM.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and mean in outlook, concerned with trivial matters: a synonym for petty.

clue.text: Give fresh instructions on radio presentation

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a show broadcast on radio is a programme

explanation.surface: Issuing new orders over a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a computer or person new instructions is to code them again, a near synonym.

clue.text: Devil's books parish condemned: not one cheats

parts.note: playing cards were called the devil's books by puritans

indicators.note: condemned means wrecked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says a letter is left out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puritan denunciation of gambling: the parish condemns cards, and none who play are honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil's books' is an old puritan name for playing cards. 'not one' drops I from PARISH, and 'condemned' rearranges PARSH into HARPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Card players who win by trickery are swindlers, people who cheat.

clue.text: Stevenson made up tale in which preliminary matter is black spot

indicators.note: preliminary matter means the opening letters of each word count here

explanation.surface: R. L. Stevenson invented a story whose opening involves the black spot, as in Treasure Island.
explanation.walkthrough: The black spot is Treasure Island's pirate summons, a lure; here it means a speck of soot.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle of soot or a fungal blemish on plants: a small dark mark.

clue.text: Circular saw changed nothing. So he took an ax

indicators.note: circular means going round, so the word saw is turned around
changed means altered, so the letters of nothing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking an axe because the circular saw achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular saw' looks like a power tool; 'Circular' turns SAW into WAS. The American 'ax' and the cherry-tree legend point to the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the young future first US president chopped down his father's cherry tree with a hatchet.

clue.text: A cat opens a world up

indicators.note: up means in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cat opening up a whole world, perhaps a key to adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'opens up'; it is the anagram signal for OPENS A WORLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wild feline of the Central Asian mountains with thick pale spotted fur.

clue.text: Second-year student hopes room can be customised

indicators.note: customising alters something to fit, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A college student hoping to personalise their dorm room.
explanation.definitionFit: In American schools and colleges, the name for a student in the second year.

clue.text: Past villain, not current

indicators.note: not says the current symbol is left out

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A former criminal now off the electricity grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past villain' reads as a former crook; 'Past' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a period, as in years before now, meaning gone by.

clue.text: A Turk trained in best college must be self-sufficient

indicators.note: in puts the reshuffled letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

indicators.note: trained means put through drill, reshaping the letters

explanation.surface: A Turk trained at a top college has to fend for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges A TURK into UTARK, which goes 'in' A1 (written AI) plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Economically independent, with a nation producing all it needs without trade.

clue.text: Ashes holder — Australia or England? They're the ones coming second

indicators.note: the letters coming second in each word are the ones to take

explanation.surface: Who holds the cricket Ashes, Australia or England, and which one finishes runner-up?
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, whose trophy is a tiny urn; here the ashes are a funeral holder's.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase holding the remains of someone cremated, as well as the small cricket trophy.

clue.text: What Eden held: empire lost by (a week's creation wasted!) weaker vessel

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the letters of empire are thrown into disorder
wasted means squandered: the letters of a week are taken away from the mixture

parts.note: the letters of the phrase a week, without its possessive ending
a ship is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Anthony Eden's empire lost, likened to God's week of creation gone to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden is Anthony Eden, UK prime minister, not the garden. EMPIRE plus WEAKER, less A WEEK, leaves letters that rearrange as PREMIER; the 'weaker vessel' contributes SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden served as British prime minister, so he held the office of the leader of government.

clue.text: He thought about the 9 being not used and not picked up

parts.note: something not used is new

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom

explanation.surface: A man pondering the fruit at 9 which went unused and was never collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 9' refers to 9 across, the fruit said to have fallen on the scientist's head and prompted his ideas on gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist Isaac, who formulated gravity after reportedly watching fruit fall from a tree.

clue.text: Silver attaches leg for conflict

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Something silver fixed to a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a contest or struggle; in literature, the central clash between characters.

clue.text: Tragic, mad Dane greeting about first father and mother …

indicators.note: about says the greeting goes round the rest

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting hail

indicators.note: tragic suggests something ruined, so the letters of mad Dane are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Hamlet, the tragic mad Dane, greets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic' rearranges MAD DANE into DAMANDE, and AVE goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the first man and woman, parents of humankind.

clue.text: Heath Robinson originally backed European gallery

parts.note: E is short for European, and being backed by the initial means that initial stands behind it

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts gallery in London

explanation.surface: Cartoonist Heath Robinson supported a European art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath Robinson' looks like the cartoonist's name; 'Heath' alone is the definition, a heather plant. R 'backed' E means R stands behind it; the ICA is a London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name for heather, the low shrub of moorland and heath.

clue.text: Difficulty about housing left confused impression

indicators.note: housing says it holds the other letter inside
about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's there's the rub

explanation.surface: A problem involving housing has left someone muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RUB into BUR, which is 'housing' L.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudged or indistinct image or memory is a hazy visual impression.

clue.text: …whom this acquaintance did for

parts.note: continuing the previous clue: the first couple were ruined by eating from the tree of this, and the word also means acquaintance with facts

explanation.surface: Following on from the first couple: the acquaintance that ruined them.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from 21 across: Adam and Eve were undone by the forbidden tree in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiarity or acquaintance with facts is awareness; the forbidden tree in Genesis bore it.

clue.text: Stick that's chewed

definitions.meaning: glue used to make things adhere
a sweet that is chewed but not swallowed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an adhesive paste for sticking and also the sweet one chews.

clue.text: In non-drinking environment Scots own a corrupting influence

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the abstainer letters surround the rest

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
ain is Scots for own

explanation.surface: Scots in a dry setting keep their own corrupting vice.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is teetotal; AIN is the Scots form of own.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace of contamination or moral corruption that spoils something.

clue.text: Red revolutionary lines surrounded Russia's capital

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: surrounded has the railway letters go round the initial

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Communist revolutionaries encircled Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks political in a clue about Russia and revolution; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright crimson shade, named after the fruit.

clue.text: Support chief town on Dornoch Firth

parts.note: main means chief or principal
Tain is a small town in the Scottish Highlands on that firth

explanation.surface: The leading town on a Highland inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Tain is a town in the Scottish Highlands, on the Dornoch Firth.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going or to provide for it financially is to support it.
